title: Microsoft Frontier program: who in your tenant gets pre-release features?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft documentation supports its enrolment, licensing, preview limitations and governance controls. The documented licensing disagreement is disclosed, and no actionable factual errors were found.

claims.claim: Frontier provides opt-in preview access to Microsoft 365 capabilities before general availability.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Frontier program gives organizations preview access to innovative and emerging capabilities in Microsoft 365 before those features reach general availability (GA).

claims.claim: Frontier covers Copilot agents and AI and non-AI experiences.
claims.quote: By opting in to Frontier, IT administrators can evaluate new Microsoft Copilot agents, review AI and non-AI powered experiences

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Frontier features are preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: Frontier features are preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: Microsoft's audience-based release model has Frontier, Standard release and Deferred release audiences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 offers a new three-tier, audience-based release model—Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release

claims.claim: Frontier is an opt-in audience for evaluating and preparing for pre-GA features.
claims.quote: Frontier (opt-in) is designed for users who want access before general availability to features to evaluate and prepare.

claims.where: What it is: Standard release audience
claims.claim: Standard release is the default release experience.
claims.quote: Standard release is the default release experience where users receive new features as soon as they're generally available.

claims.where: What it is: Standard release audience
claims.claim: Standard release delivers features as soon as they are generally available.
claims.quote: Standard release is the default release experience where users receive new features as soon as they're generally available.

claims.where: What it is: Deferred release audience
claims.claim: Deferred release delays deferred-eligible major updates.
claims.quote: Deferred release lets you delay deferred-eligible major updates for specific users for approximately 30 days after rollout to the Standard release audience begins.

claims.where: What it is: Deferred release audience
claims.claim: The Deferred delay is approximately 30 days after Standard release rollout begins.
claims.quote: Deferred release lets you delay deferred-eligible major updates for specific users for approximately 30 days after rollout to the Standard release audience begins.

claims.claim: Users can be enrolled in Frontier while also assigned to Standard or Deferred release.
claims.quote: You can opt in users to both Frontier preview and assign them to Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: The existing Standard or Deferred preference determines GA delivery for features outside Frontier.
claims.quote: For features that aren't part of Frontier, the user's existing Standard release or Deferred release preference determines when they receive features at GA.

claims.claim: Frontier is managed at tenant level.
claims.quote: Frontier is managed at the tenant level.

claims.claim: An administrator turns on Frontier and controls its user audience.
claims.quote: To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On. Choose how Frontier access is assigned in your organization:

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: All users assigns Frontier features and agents across the tenant, subject to product eligibility.
claims.quote: All users - All users automatically receive Frontier features and agents.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Specific users and groups assigns Frontier only to the specified audience.
claims.quote: Specific users and groups - Only specified users and groups automatically receive Frontier features and agents.

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users need licences providing access to the products they preview.
claims.quote: Assign users licenses that provide access to the products you want them to preview.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Governance controls
claims.claim: Agent controls independently govern availability of Frontier agents.
claims.quote: The Frontier admin control doesn't override the settings configured in the Agent section of the admin center.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: New Frontier agents published from 29 March 2026 require Frontier enrolment.
claims.quote: Starting March 29, 2026, newly published Frontier agents are available only to Frontier-enrolled users.

claims.claim: Frontier agents published before 29 March 2026 remain accessible to users with a Microsoft Copilot licence without Frontier enrolment.
claims.quote: Frontier agents published before this date continue to be accessible to all users with a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Frontier agents appear in Microsoft Copilot's Agent Store with (Frontier) in their names.
claims.quote: Frontier agents are available to them from the Agent store in Microsoft Copilot. Search for "Built by Microsoft", and Frontier program agents are displayed with (Frontier) in the name.

claims.claim: Frontier feature and agent availability can take up to three hours to propagate.
claims.quote: It might take three hours for Frontier features and agents to be available to users.

claims.claim: The Get started page does not state an on/off default for a tenant that has never changed Frontier.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier default get-started-frontier; Frontier enrollment Turn on Frontier default enabled disabled. Read Get started with the Microsoft Frontier Program and Configure new Standard and Deferred release options in full; neither states Frontier's untouched-tenant on/off default.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; What to check
claims.claim: Enrolment requires AI Administrator, Security Administrator or Office Apps Administrator.
claims.quote: You need an account that includes one of the following roles: AI Administrator; Security Administrator; Office Apps Administrator

claims.claim: A Microsoft Copilot licence is not required to enrol users in the expanded Frontier program.
claims.quote: With the expansion of Frontier across Microsoft 365 previews to include both AI and non-AI features, a Microsoft Copilot license isn't required to enroll users in Frontier.

claims.claim: Copilot Frontier features require a Copilot licence or a licence including access to Copilot.
claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Copilot, users need a Microsoft Copilot license or a license that includes access to Copilot.

claims.claim: Enrolled users without Copilot licensing are not shown Copilot-related Frontier features.
claims.quote: Users enrolled in Frontier without a Microsoft Copilot license aren't presented with Copilot-related Frontier features.

claims.claim: Teams-related Frontier features require a licence including Teams.
claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Microsoft Teams, users need a license that includes access to Teams.

claims.claim: The Get started prerequisites list roles and product licences but name no separate Frontier fee.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier program enrollment licensing fee. Read the Get started page's complete Prerequisites and its closing payment terms: prerequisites name roles and product licences, not a separate enrolment fee; closing terms allow paid experiences.

claims.claim: Certain Frontier experiences may be available only on a paid basis.
claims.quote: Certain Frontier experiences may only be available on a paid basis.

claims.claim: Microsoft refers readers to its Copilot Credits Guide for credit consumption requirements.
claims.quote: Copilot credit consumption requirements are described in the Microsoft Copilot Credits Guide.

claims.claim: Once the unified experience is available, admins no longer need Copilot licensing to opt in through either enrolment experience.
claims.quote: Once the unified release preferences experience is available, admins will no longer be required to have a license that includes Copilot to opt in to Frontier via the existing experience or the new unified release preferences experience.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 Frontier FAQ gives a different answer, directing tenants missing Copilot Frontier to purchase Copilot or E7.
claims.quote: I don't see Copilot Frontier under Copilot Settings. | Purchase a Microsoft 365 Copilot license or Microsoft E7 license if you don't already have one.

claims.claim: An admin account needs corresponding product licensing for full access; some Frontier settings and agents otherwise may not appear.
claims.quote: Verify that your own admin account has also has a corresponding license for products to ensure full access to Frontier AI settings and agents. Some Frontier settings and agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not appear.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Preview terms
claims.claim: Frontier experiences may be modified, suspended or discontinued.
claims.quote: As preview features, Frontier experiences may be modified, suspended, or discontinued

claims.claim: Standard support commitments or SLAs may not cover Frontier experiences.
claims.quote: may not be covered by standard support commitments or service level agreements

claims.claim: Additional Frontier-specific preview terms may apply.
claims.quote: may be subject to additional Frontier-specific preview terms where applicable.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Compliance coverage; What to check
claims.claim: HIPAA Business Associate Agreement coverage is not included for Frontier experiences.
claims.quote: HIPAA Business Associate Agreement coverage is not included for Frontier experiences.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Compliance coverage; What to check
claims.claim: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27001 requirements.
claims.quote: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27001, ISO 27002, or ISO 27018 requirements.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Compliance coverage; What to check
claims.claim: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27002 requirements.
claims.quote: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27001, ISO 27002, or ISO 27018 requirements.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Compliance coverage; What to check
claims.claim: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27018 requirements.
claims.quote: Frontier features do not comply with ISO 27001, ISO 27002, or ISO 27018 requirements.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Agent controls; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Frontier agent disabled in the Agent view is unavailable regardless of the user's Frontier enrolment.
claims.quote: If an admin turned off a Frontier agent in the Agent view, that agent isn't available to users, regardless of a user's Frontier enrollment.

claims.claim: Frontier never enables AI providers on the administrator's behalf.
claims.quote: Frontier will never enable AI providers on your behalf.

claims.claim: A feature requiring an AI provider such as Anthropic is unusable until the administrator enables that provider.
claims.quote: Some Frontier features and agents require access to large language models from AI providers, such as Anthropic. If the corresponding AI provider isn't enabled by you, the Frontier feature will not be usable for you or your users.

claims.claim: Frontier is currently unavailable in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: For customers in GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments, Standard release (general availability) remains the supported release option following the retirement of Targeted release. Currently, Deferred release and Frontier aren't available in government cloud environments.

claims.claim: The unified enrolment control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences > Turn on Frontier.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Settings > Org settings. Under the Organization profile tab, select Release preferences. To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: The existing enrolment path is Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier > Turn on Frontier.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Settings. Select the View all tab. In the Search all Copilot settings search bar, type "Frontier". Select Copilot Frontier. To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually from mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually in mid-November 2026, so it might not be available in your organization yet.

claims.claim: The existing Frontier enrolment experience remains when the unified experience becomes available.
claims.quote: When the unified release preferences experience becomes available, the existing experience for opting in to Frontier preview within the Microsoft 365 admin center will still exist.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for the tenant's Frontier enrolment and user/group assignment control.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier enrollment Graph PowerShell; Frontier program enrollment automation API; Frontier tenant enrollment assignment API. Read get-started-frontier, utcm-copilot-resources and utcm-agent-resources: OCPS frontier toggles web-app access, not enrolment assignments.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built Frontier agent access is controlled at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access > Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access. Verify that Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft is checked. This setting allows the use of Microsoft Frontier agents.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft controls users' installation of Microsoft-built agents, including Frontier agents.
claims.quote: Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft - Enables users to install agents and plugins created by Microsoft.

claims.claim: Users still see Microsoft-built agents when that setting is disabled.
claims.quote: Users see agents and plugins built by Microsoft even if you disable the setting, but they can't install those agents and plugins.

claims.claim: Users cannot install Microsoft-built agents while that setting is disabled.
claims.quote: Users see agents and plugins built by Microsoft even if you disable the setting, but they can't install those agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the allowedagenttypes desired-state baseline using applyOnce.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: Preview TCM supports mode applyOnce for applying Agent resource baselines once.
claims.quote: TCM drift remediation and applyOnce monitors change workload configuration on behalf of the signed-in administrator. These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: The Microsoft-built agent access baseline uses resourceType microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes.
claims.quote:
"displayName": "Allowed agent types",
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes",

claims.claim: The Agent baseline resource version is 1.
claims.quote: All resources on this page use resourceVersion: 1 and are singletons.

claims.claim: The baseline valueObject.areMicrosoftAppsAllowed property is a writable Boolean controlling Microsoft-built apps, agents and plugins.
claims.quote: areMicrosoftAppsAllowed | Write | Boolean | Indicates whether apps, agents, and plugins built by Microsoft are allowed.

claims.claim: Per-agent blocking is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock. In the Block agent or Unblock agent pane that opens, select either Block agent or Unblock agent

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: The Block action restricts the selected agent across the whole organisation.
claims.quote: Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its use.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The package block API is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The block API needs delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: The block API is unavailable in US Government clouds.
claims.quote:
Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet

claims.claim: Admins can directly install an agent by selecting it in Agents > All agents, assigning its Users tab audience and selecting Install.
claims.quote: Go to Agents > All agents. Select the agent you want to install. In the Users tab, add the specific users or security groups that you want to use this agent. In the agent flyout, select Install.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra ID security groups can target Frontier pilot users.
claims.quote: Use a Microsoft Entra ID security group to target specific users who can access Frontier agents. This approach helps you validate experiences with a small group before broad rollout.

claims.claim: Users receiving directly deployed Frontier agents must also be assigned in Frontier Admin Control.
claims.quote: You can install and pin specific agents for select users or groups directly rather than users needing to search the Agent store. This method helps users start using Frontier agents more quickly. You must assign these users in Frontier Admin Control

claims.claim: Microsoft documents UpdateTenantSettings for Microsoft 365 Copilot setting changes.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot admin activities
Updated a Copilot setting | UpdateTenantSettings | An admin (or system on behalf of an admin) updated a Copilot setting.

claims.claim: The audit activities table does not name a Frontier-specific operation.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities Frontier UpdateTenantSettings. Fetched the full Audit log activities page and searched its text for Frontier, UpdateTenantSettings and UpdatedTenantSettings; no Frontier entry appears.
